hashbang.comment: §1.1 HashbangComment — admitted only as the very first characters of the input.
hashbang.name: comment.line.shebang.vertex

triple-slash-directive.comment: §13.2 TripleSlashDirective. Unlisted in the fork diff, so inherited unchanged — and unexercised by any spec document.
triple-slash-directive.name: comment.line.triple-slash.vertex

check-pragma.comment: §13.3 CheckPragma. Inherited unchanged, so the spelling is still `@ts-`, not `@vtx-`.

namespace-header.comment: §7 NamespaceHeader — file-scoped, first item in the CompilationUnit, cannot nest or be re-opened. The braced NamespaceBody form is removed, so `namespace` never introduces a block.

use-directive.comment: §13.1 UseDirective: use Identifier. Takes no arguments — no version, no parens, never a string. The grammar admits any Identifier; the four slots below are the ones the build actually checks (use.md), so they get distinct scopes and anything else falls through to the generic arm.

patterns.comment: Memory model slot — optional, implied by every platform.
Platform slot — fixes the numeric table and the foreign resolver.
Runtime slot — native platforms only; noentry requires nostd.
Accelerated backend slot — gates kernel func / graph func bodies.
Grammatical but not a known slot value. Not marked invalid — that is a build-time check, not a parse error.

import-declaration.comment: §4.1 ImportDeclaration: import ImportSpec | import ( {ImportSpec} ). ImportSpec is [ImportAlias] StringLiteral — no named bindings, no FromClause, no `from`/`require`/`defer`. An ImportAlias is therefore only ever the identifier immediately preceding a specifier string, which is why this is scoped to the declaration rather than matched loose.

patterns.comment: ImportAlias: Identifier or `_`. The group needs no separator — after a spec's StringLiteral the next token is a StringLiteral, an Identifier/_, or `)`.
§12 AmbientStructDeclaration: declare struct BindingIdentifier — a layout-free type, legal only in pointer positions.
§5.2 FunctionDeclaration: {Decorator} {FunctionModifier} func BindingIdentifier CallSignature. FunctionModifier is kernel|graph; the async and generator variants take the function -> func swap only.

§5.1 TypeAliasDeclaration. Unlisted in the fork diff, so inherited — but main_llama.vs asserts there is no alias form. Highlighted pending confirmation; if the alias really is gone, delete this arm and `type` reverts to an ordinary identifier.
§6 DestructorDeclaration — no parameters, no modifiers, mandatory Block. Legal only under `native`; illegal under `host` on both android and js.

ambient-module.comment: §12 AmbientModuleDeclaration: declare module StringLiteral. Scoped as a begin/end so the scheme prefix is only ever recognised in specifier position, never in an arbitrary string that happens to start with `cpp:`.

module-specifier-double.comment: Scheme prefixes cost zero grammar — they live inside the StringLiteral, and an unknown scheme is a resolution error rather than a parse error. The live set is dynamic: (windows/linux/darwin, dlopen at first use), framework: (darwin), and cpp: (C++ mangling). `objc:` and `jvm:` are gone: darwin spells Objective-C access through framework:, and android takes a bare package name with no scheme at all.
module-specifier-double.name: string.quoted.double.module.vertex

decorators.comment: §11. Decorator itself is unedited; what changed is where {Decorator} may appear — FunctionDeclaration (§5), StructDeclaration and StructElement (§6). Known spellings: @packed, @align(N), @bits(N), @inline, @objc. There is no @android or @jvm — `use android` says it once per file instead.

member-name-string.comment: A StringLiteral in member position is a name, not data: JVM overload descriptors ("sample002(Ljava/lang/String;)V"), Objective-C selectors ("sample002:sample003:"), and C++ operators ("operator+"). Covers both the declaration site and the a["..."](b) call site.

string-single.comment: Vertex has no character literal — 'A' is a String in TS and stayed one here.
string-single.name: string.quoted.single.vertex

string-escape.comment: §1.6.2 EscapeSequence, LineContinuation, and the NonEscapeCharacter fallback.

regex.comment: §1.6.4. RegularExpressionLiteral survives — §1.8 names it among the tokens that can end a statement. The goal symbol is chosen by the preceding token, so the lookbehind whitelists tokens that cannot end an expression. `of` and `from` are absent because they are no longer keywords.
regex.name: string.regexp.vertex

numbers.comment: §1.6.1. The first DecimalLiteral alternative requires fractional digits, so `1.` is not a literal and `0..10` lexes as 0 .. 10 rather than 0. . 10 — which is what makes the range form work without a lexer hack. Underscores are separators only and carry no grouping convention. No legacy octal.

patterns.comment: `null` is load-bearing in type position too — absence is always an explicit union at every foreign boundary. Scoped as a constant in both positions, matching TS.
patterns.name: constant.language.null.vertex

predefined-types.comment: §2 PredefinedType. Two entries replaced: number -> int, boolean -> bool. `void` is listed here rather than as the void operator: `: void` is ubiquitous in Vertex and the unary operator is unexercised, so type position wins the collision. This block sits above #keywords for that reason.
predefined-types.name: support.type.primitive.vertex

numeric-type-names.comment: §2 — these are ordinary TypeIdentifiers, not PredefinedType entries. That distinction is exactly what makes int32(a) parse as a CallExpression. Highlighted as types, so a conversion call reads as a type name followed by an argument list, which is what it is.
numeric-type-names.name: support.type.numeric.vertex

builtin-types.comment: Pointer family (native, plus weak_ptr as the lone survivor under android), contiguous storage, and the accelerated types. All lowercase, so the capitalized #type-name heuristic below would miss every one of them.
builtin-types.name: support.type.builtin.vertex

builtin-functions.comment: native.md §2-§3 and §8. Layout introspection, allocation, placement construction, pointer casts, explicit load/store, and the kernel compile/launch pair. Ordered longest-first for readability; \b already prevents alloc from shadowing alloc_uninit.
builtin-functions.name: support.function.builtin.vertex

accelerator-intrinsics.comment: native.md §8 — thread-context intrinsics, legal only inside a kernel func body.
accelerator-intrinsics.name: support.variable.intrinsic.vertex

keywords.comment: §1.5. Deliberately absent: `function`, `of`, `from`, `require`, `defer` — each removed from the keyword set, so each is now an ordinary identifier and must not be highlighted. `number` and `boolean` are orphaned contextual entries and behave the same way.

patterns.comment: §8. `if let` binds one identifier, no patterns, and `let` is contextually reserved by position after `if`.

§8 — `case X:` and fallthrough are gone (comma lists replace grouped fallthrough); for-in is the sole iteration form. try/catch/finally/throw are inherited unedited but semantically unexercised: Vertex does not unwind, and foreign failure is always a return union.
patterns.name: keyword.control.flow.vertex

patterns.comment: Still reserved (§1.5), but the WithStatement production is removed (§8) — reserved with nothing to derive.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.reserved.vertex

patterns.comment: `readonly` occupies two binding sites, disambiguated by position — member modifier before an identifier, prefix type operator after a `:`. `mutating` is contextual, legal only following a `:` in parameter, return, or this-parameter position, so `var mutating = 0` stays a legal binding. Neither distinction is expressible here; both take the one modifier scope.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.vertex

function-call.comment: Placed above #type-name so a capitalized call reads as a call — Win32 and framework entry points are capitalized, and Sample001() construction is a call too. A bare capitalized identifier still falls through to the type heuristic.

type-name.comment: Heuristic: capitalized identifiers are type references. The grammar has no such rule — this is presentation only.
type-name.name: entity.name.type.vertex

operators.comment: §1.7 Punctuator. `>>`, `>>>`, `>>=` and `>>>=` are NOT tokens: a `>` is only ever matched alone, so compound shift forms surface as adjacent `>` operators, exactly as the grammar writes them (`> >`, `> >=`). `..` is matched after `...` and before `.` for maximal munch. `?.` is optional chaining only when not followed by a decimal digit.

patterns.comment: §1.8 — `;` remains a legal terminal everywhere, it is simply no longer required. Terminator insertion is rule-driven, not error-driven.
patterns.name: punctuation.terminator.statement.vertex
